name: Mountain climber
summary: From a high plank, drive your knees toward your chest one at a time. Bodyweight cardio that also trains the trunk to hold steady.
setup: Start in a high plank: hands under your shoulders, arms straight, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Push the floor away so your upper back is full, not sunk between the shoulder blades.

steps.text: Pull one knee toward your chest, landing the toes lightly under your hip if you can.
Send that foot back and bring the other knee in. Hips stay level, at plank height.
Keep a steady rhythm you can hold for the whole interval. Speed only counts if the plank holds.

jointCues.cue: Stacked over the wrists, pushing the floor away.
jointCues.why: Shoulders behind the hands shift the load to the wrists; sinking between the blades strains the shoulder.

jointCues.cue: Level with the shoulders. Do not bounce them up toward the ceiling.
jointCues.why: High hips turn it into a pike and take the work off the abs.

jointCues.cue: Neutral, ribs down, a slight round between the shoulder blades.
jointCues.why: Letting the lower back sag puts it into a loaded arch every rep.

jointCues.cue: Drive toward the chest, in line with the hip.
jointCues.why: A full knee drive works the hip flexors and abs through their range.

breathing: Breathe out on one or two knee drives, in on the next one or two. Keep breathing; holding the breath makes the interval much harder.
tempo: Intervals: 20 to 40 s on, equal rest

mistakes.fix: Slow down until you can keep the hips at plank height.
Shift your weight forward so the shoulders stay over the wrists.
Touch the toes down under the hip each time.

cues.text: Hips level with the shoulders: no bouncing
